newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI to continue buying dollar - Stanchart poll.
newsitem.headline: India RBI to continue buying dollar - Stanchart poll.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to continue its intervention in the foreign exchange market to prevent the rupee's rise against the dollar, a poll of authorised dealers by Standard Chartered Bank treasury showed.
"Do you think the RBI will stop buying dollars in the month of August in the face of increasing M3 growth?" the bank asked the dealers, in a poll on Friday.

The RBI has been intervening in the foreign exchange market for over six months, buying dollars to arrest the rupee's rise in the face of continued capital inflows and poor importer demand for the U.S. currency.
RBI intervention has been adding to the money supply as RBI's dollar purchases release rupees into the system.
According to latest RBI data, M3 money growth rose to 16.8 percent on June 20 compared to 16.6 percent on June 6.
The RBI has set a target of 15.0-15.5 percent growth in money supply for 1997/98 (April-March).
Many dealers say RBI is intervening in the forex market reluctantly because of its implications on money supply growth.
On Friday, RBI was in the market again, buying dollars from banks approaching it.
